newsitem.title: USA: Venoco buys Mobil California offshore field.
newsitem.headline: Venoco buys Mobil California offshore field.

text.p: Venoco Inc over the weekend bought the South Ellwood offshore oil field in California from Mobil Exploration & Producing US Inc for an undisclosed amount, the company confirmed Monday.

California-based Venoco, an independent oil company, said the 30-year-old field produces about 5,000 barrels-per-day (bpd) of oil. Daily production of natural gas stands at three million cubic feet (MMcf) for the field.
The sale includes an offshore platform and related facilities, the company said.

Mobil sold South Ellwood because the property was far-removed from its core oil fields in California's Kern County, which recently merged with Shell Oil Co's California assets, a Venoco spokesman said.
The company, with about $125 million in assets, plans one or two more U.S. acquisitions before year-end, the spokesman said.
Venoco, a private company headquartered in Santa Barbara, Calif., owns 10 oil fields in the western U.S.
